headline: Montana Teen's Roping Skills Save Drowning Man on Yellowstone River
meta_description: A 14-year-old ranch kid used his lasso skills to rescue a man clinging to a cooler in the Yellowstone River, catching him on the first try.
summary_short: A 14-year-old Montana teen who spent his afternoons practicing with a lasso rescued a drowning man on the Yellowstone River during Fourth of July weekend.
body:
When a raft and paddle board struck a bridge pier near Greycliff, Montana, four people tumbled into the Yellowstone River. Three made it to shore on their own, but the fourth clung helplessly to a cooler, drifting swiftly downstream. That's when Jory Thomas, 14, heard the screaming while at his grandparents' house along the river and acted without hesitation. He emptied his pockets, grabbed his lariat, waded chest-deep into the water, and caught the man around the arm and neck on his first throw—exactly as he'd practiced all summer on cattle at brandings and ropers' gatherings.

Thomas had only recently become obsessed with roping. "Every afternoon when it cools off, I go out and rope the roping dummy," he told local news, describing the dedication that made his split-second instinct possible. A bystander rushed to help him reel the man back to shore. What made those seconds critical was the river itself: the swift current in that section quickly funnels toward rapids, logjams, and other obstacles that can easily claim lives. Sweet Grass County Sheriff Alan Ronneberg later told reporters that without Thomas's intervention, "the chances of this individual not making it to shore were very slim."

Thomas's father, a veteran volunteer firefighter, had already called 911 when the screaming started, and a sheriff's deputy arrived within three minutes. But by then, the boy and the bystander had already done the work. Afterward, Thomas's grandmother Sandy recalled her grandson climbing out of the water and saying simply: "I think I just saved a life." It was a moment of clarity born not from heroic fantasy, but from the ordinary discipline of a teenager who loved what he did—and happened to be exactly where he needed to be.
quick_facts: 14-year-old Jory Thomas caught a drowning man with his lasso on first try
Rescue happened on Yellowstone River near Greycliff, Sweet Grass County, Montana
Man was clinging to cooler in swift current leading to dangerous rapids
Thomas had started roping cattle seriously that same summer
